subject: Hosting options & security asks — HealthSync discovery
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
To: Emma Crawford <emma.crawford@healthsync.com>, Kevin Lee <kevin.lee@healthsync.com>
Date: 2026-12-15T18:10:00-08:00
Subject: Recap: Hosting options & security asks — HealthSync discovery

Emma / Kevin,

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed so we have the same page: 

Summary of hosting options (high-level):
- Hosted API (Redwood-hosted): fastest to production, shared multi-tenant runtime, encrypted in transit + at rest, SOC2 controls in-place. Good if you need fast time-to-value and lower operational overhead.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs): single-tenant pool, predictable throughput and deterministic latency. Data isolation at the compute layer; good middle-ground for higher throughput with contractual isolation.
- Private deployment (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed networking and control plane; recommended for strict regulatory requirements (BAA + additional audit controls). Longer lead time.

Key security/compliance items you flagged:
- HIPAA / BAA required for any PHI processing or storage
- SOC2 Type II report and pen-test attestation requested by your InfoSec team
- Data residency: prefer US-only (us-east-1)
- Audit log retention and eDiscovery / legal-hold requirements

Asks from our side to help scope:
1) Estimated QPS / monthly token volume and expected peak concurrency.
2) Confirm whether HealthSync will send PHI in requests or store outputs (PHI at rest) — both matter for recommended hosting path.
3) Retention period for logs / records and whether you require immutable records / legal-hold.
4) Any required sub-processors or third-party attestations you must review.

Immediate next steps (proposed):
- I will send our SOC2 Type II report, a draft BAA, and a short hosting comparison doc (attached).
- If you confirm PHI will be processed and you need a BAA, we should schedule a short security deep-dive this week with our Solutions engineer + Security (30–45m).
- If you need Private VPC/on-prem, we can scope network requirements and provide an initial timeline and cost estimate.

Attachments: hosting-options-summary.pdf (short comparison)

Proposed times for the security deep-dive: Thu 12/17 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 12/18 9:00–10:00 PT. Let me know what works.

Thanks — talk soon.

Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0199

From: Emma Crawford <emma.crawford@healthsync.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-16T09:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Recap: Hosting options & security asks — HealthSync discovery

Sergio,

Thanks for the recap — that matches what we talked about. A few clarifying items from our InfoSec/procurement side so we can move quickly: 

1) BAA: We cannot begin any testing or transmit PHI until a BAA is in place. Please send the draft BAA and indicate the path/owner for execution (DocuSign preferred).
2) SOC2: We need the most recent SOC2 Type II report and the scope (services included). If you provide a SOC2 portal or a download link that would be ideal.
3) Encryption: Confirm TLS versions for in-transit and whether server-side encryption uses KMS-managed keys (and options for customer-managed keys).
4) Sub-processors: Please provide a current sub-processor list and the cadence of notification for changes.
5) Pen testing: Do you have a pen-test attestation or summary for the past 12 months? Whether third-party or internal is fine.
6) Data residency: We require US-only hosting in us-east-1 for now.
7) Audit logs / retention: Our legal team is asking for 7-year retention on audit logs and the ability to export logs for eDiscovery. Is that supported?

Procurement timeline: We are targeting a commercial decision by the end of this quarter (Q4). If Redwood can provide the SOC2 report, BAA draft, sub-processor list, and a high-level timeline for Dedicated vs Private by EOD Thursday, that will help us move to legal review quickly.

If we can get those items, Kevin and I will coordinate a 30–45m technical deep-dive with your Solutions/Security folks.

Best,
Emma
Emma Crawford
Head of Platform Security | HealthSync

What we'll provide (and timeline):
- SOC2 Type II report (PDF) + secure Drive link: I will authorize Monica to share the redacted report today. (attachment: SOC2_Report_Redwood_2026.pdf) — delivery: within 24 business hours.
- BAA draft: I reviewed a standard BAA template and produced a DocuSign-ready draft (BAA_Draft_HealthSync_v1.docx). Minor edits on liability/indemnity; I will send the DocuSign link to Sergio to forward to HealthSync.
- Sub-processor list + pen-test attestation: Monica will attach subprocessor_list.csv and the latest pen-test attestation (summary) today.
- Encryption/KMS: Aditya, is our KMS offering customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private? If yes, provide short bullet we can send to the customer. If not, provide recommended mitigations.
- Audit logs / retention: We support exporting immutable audit logs. Seven-year storage is not default; we can support it via long-term archive (S3 Glacier) and retention policy — will provide estimated storage and costs (rough $/GB/year) in the cost estimate.

Operational timelines (high level):
- Hosted API: immediate (hours) once commercial terms complete; no BAA required for demo traffic but BAA required before PHI handling.
- Dedicated capacity: provisioning typically 4–6 weeks (increasing to 6–8 weeks if specific PCI-like network isolation is required).
- Private VPC/on-prem: 6–10 weeks depending on network readiness and customer provisioning windows.

Next steps for customer-facing message: Sergio, send the SOC2 link + BAA DocuSign + sub-processor list and propose the security deep-dive (we recommend Laura + Aditya + Solutions lead on the call). Suggest slots Thu 12/17 10:00 PT or Fri 12/18 9:00 PT (be mindful some of those are close — we can offer next week as a fallback).
